PRODUCT
A personal Windows desktop prototype faithfully capturing Microsoft Sticky Notes’ essential experience: a searchable notes list plus independently opened sticky-note windows. Warm colored notes, compact title bars, readable text, simple formatting and unobtrusive controls. Support drawing within each note and exchange with the installed tldraw Desktop. Work fully offline; no Microsoft sign-in or cloud sync. Development prototype only; do not claim licensed production release.

DRAWING + DESKTOP INTEGRATION
Each note has its own embedded editable tldraw drawing, with undo/redo and persisted drawing state. Switching notes never mixes drawings. Publish a selected note/drawing to an explicitly chosen existing tldraw Desktop canvas; update that published item without duplicate creation. Import a selected Desktop note/drawing as a local note. REQUIRED BEHAVIOR
Create, edit, format and delete text notes; choose seven note colors; search text case-insensitively; list and reopen existing notes. Independently move/resize/open/close multiple note windows. CONCEPT SKETCH — DELIBERATELY UNRESOLVED

              [ A ♠ ]      [ 7 ♥ ]         +         aim / shoot

                            ?

                  ONE COHERENT PLAYABLE LOOP

How do blackjack decisions change the action?
How does shooting change the blackjack situation?
Which interpretation feels fun, clear and small enough to finish?

These are design questions for the agent, not prescribed mechanics.

THE CONCEPT
“Scribble blackjack, but make it a shooter.”

A small, enjoyable offline desktop game with a hand-drawn, animated scribble aesthetic. Blackjack and shooting must combine into one understandable game. Decide how the combination works. Cards, risk and the spirit of blackjack should meaningfully affect play; shooting should be an active part of the experience. The player should discover a satisfying loop quickly.

DELIVERY BOUNDARIES
One small local desktop game, runnable offline with documented launch instructions. Fictional stakes only; no real-money play, accounts, purchases or cloud dependency. Supply all required assets locally. Keep the scope small enough to finish.

Teach controls and the blackjack/shooting interaction inside the game. Provide a complete playable loop with feedback, a clear outcome and a way to replay. Animated hand-drawn presentation is part of the brief.

OPEN DESIGN SPACE
Choose the perspective, controls, rules, pacing, visual language and relationship between blackjack and combat. Invent the interaction rather than copying a supplied solution.

There is no prescribed deck size, payout model, enemy pattern, engine, architecture or ticket breakdown. Exact casino blackjack rules are optional. Explain the rules you choose and make the finished game follow them consistently.
Scribble blackjack — but make it a shooter

OBSERVABLE ACCEPTANCE
□ Actual desktop game launches and can be played offline.
□ Shooting is playable; blackjack meaningfully affects the same gameplay loop.
□ Rules and controls can be understood without reading source.
□ The selected rules behave consistently; important transitions and rapid/repeated input are tested.
□ A complete loop reaches an outcome and can restart cleanly.
□ Scribble visual style and animation are visible and coherent.
□ Deliver launch instructions, design rationale and verification evidence.

No single reference mechanic or visual solution is required.

No publication, accounts or paid services. Preserve all attempts, failures, reviews, interventions and reported/unknown usage. This page is the complete product input; previous solutions and grading fixtures are withheld. Environment, models and budget are pinned by the benchmark runner. Future requirement changes create a new version; do not silently change this brief.

PRODUCT
A small offline batch-processing app with a usable graphical client, a local service API and independently restartable workers. Submit sales CSV files, watch jobs progress, inspect results, cancel work and retry failures. Support at least two concurrent workers and several queued jobs. Clear labels and trustworthy state matter more than decoration. No cloud, authentication or distributed-machine deployment required. Database, framework, queue mechanism and ticket decomposition are your choices.

FIXED JOB WORKLOAD
UTF-8 CSV header: category,quantity,unit_price_cents. Category is nonempty text; quantity is a positive integer; unit price is a nonnegative integer. Support quoted CSV fields. Reject malformed rows with an actionable diagnostic.
For valid input return row count, total quantity, exact total sales in cents, and sales totals by category. Each row contributes quantity × unit_price_cents. Never use approximate money arithmetic. Include small sample files and documented finite upload/row limits; reject oversize input clearly.

CLIENT + API BEHAVIOR
Submit a file; list jobs; inspect status, progress, attempt history, diagnostics and completed results. Show queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled truthfully. API can perform the same core actions without the client. Progress is bounded and meaningful; errors are not successes.
Submission retries with the same client request ID and same payload return the same job; conflicting payload under that ID is rejected. Failed jobs can be explicitly retried with retained attempt history. Finished results remain available after restarts.

CONCURRENCY + RECOVERY
Multiple workers must not publish conflicting or duplicate results for one job. Kill a worker mid-job: the job is recoverable, never silently lost or stuck forever. Restart service/workers with pending jobs: retain jobs, history and completed outputs.
Cancel queued/running jobs; cancellation and completion races yield one coherent final outcome. A cancelled job cannot later publish success. Disconnect/reconnect client: show connection loss and reconcile actual state. Preserve evidence of failures and retries. Document bounded recovery/retry policy; replay-safe effects matter more than a claimed exactly-once execution label.

OBSERVABLE ACCEPTANCE
□ Real client/service/two workers launch locally from documented commands.
□ Several CSV jobs produce independently checkable exact results.
□ Repeated submission is idempotent; conflicting reuse fails.
□ Malformed/oversize input fails clearly without breaking other jobs.
□ Worker kill and service restart preserve/recover pending work.
□ Two workers cannot duplicate or overwrite a final result.
□ Cancellation/completion races and explicit retry preserve coherent state/history.
□ Client reconnect shows actual state and results.
□ Automated API/recovery checks and actual graphical-client evidence are supplied.
